insights.claim: Identity enforcement is configuration-gated rather than structurally guaranteed, meaning authentication can be entirely bypassed in local/development mode.
insights.reasoning: The RequiresIdentityHeaders() check at server.go:430 gates all identity enforcement. When this returns false (local mode or unconfigured), API endpoints for evaluations/jobs/collections/providers accept requests without any user or tenant identification. Platform operators deploying eval-hub must ensure configuration enables identity enforcement in production.

insights.claim: Eval-hub has no Kubernetes Service or ingress manifests; service exposure is entirely platform-delegated.
insights.reasoning: The Dockerfile declares io.openshift.expose-services='' and no kustomization.yaml exists in the repository. This means the RHOAI operator or platform installer is responsible for creating the Kubernetes Service, Route, or Gateway resources that expose eval-hub to cluster consumers. Platform architects must track this dependency in the operator's manifest set.

insights.claim: All four Go binaries use GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime with dynamic linking, establishing strong FIPS compliance posture at both build and application layers.
insights.reasoning: The strictfipsruntime experiment flag routes Go crypto operations through the system OpenSSL at runtime. Combined with CGO_ENABLED=1 and UBI9 base images, this satisfies both the check-payload gate (dynamic linking + OpenSSL present) and application-level crypto correctness (TLS 1.2+ minimum, no non-FIPS cipher suites detected). The MLflow client explicitly sets MinVersion=TLS1.2 and MaxVersion=TLS1.3.
